nodes.label: Ctrl+Alt+L global hotkey
nodes.rationale: Registered with null window handle on its own message pump so it fires while overlay is hidden.

nodes.label: Loopback WebSocket control API
nodes.rationale: Dynamic OS-chosen port so no well-known port to predict; JSON only for control, never for game packets.

nodes.label: Daemon events (peer.connected vs peer.state)
nodes.rationale: peer.connected is distinct because channel-open and something-came-back are different facts.

nodes.label: Ed25519 peer identity (identity.key)
nodes.rationale: Not used to sign DTLS cert (Pion only accepts RSA/ECDSA); HMAC-authenticated SDP already pins the DTLS fingerprint. Platform keystore is a future requirement.

nodes.label: LanBaz (LAN gaming over the internet)
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted, open-source (MIT) alternative to Radmin VPN/Hamachi; game traffic flows peer to peer so LanBaz never needs to see it.

nodes.label: In-game overlay (non-injected window)
nodes.rationale: No DLL injection to avoid anti-cheat flags; cost: cannot cover DirectX exclusive fullscreen.

nodes.label: Signalling / ControlTransport / ControlReceiver / StateReporter
nodes.rationale: Kept beside Transport rather than inside it so a raw-UDP transport cannot return a fake success; non-capable transports report a clean capability failure.

nodes.label: Pairing code (LBZ-, offer/answer)
nodes.rationale: ~2,400 chars because the ICE credentials/SDP are the code; intended transfer is clipboard or lanbaz:// URI.

nodes.label: Peer binary framing header
nodes.rationale: Authenticity comes from DTLS; envelope carries no crypto material.

nodes.label: Room server (optional self-hosted rendezvous)
nodes.rationale: Only introduces peers; never carries game traffic; optional and self-hosted first.

nodes.label: Layered architecture (Game -> Virtual LAN -> Router -> Peer Manager -> Transport)
nodes.norm_label: layered architecture (game -> virtual lan -> router -> peer manager -> transport)
nodes.rationale: Nothing above the transport line may learn which transport carries a packet, so WebRTC/UDP/relay are swappable without edits above.

nodes.label: Peer state machine (core/internal/peer)
nodes.rationale: Exactly one owner: two state machines could disagree; transport reports mechanical facts, transition table refuses non-forward transitions so late Pion callbacks cannot resurrect a dead link.

nodes.label: Serverless constraint
nodes.rationale: No room server: offer and answer must travel inside codes, revocation is host-side rotation.

nodes.label: Decode -> Verify -> Validate order
nodes.rationale: Checking expiry before signature would let an attacker extend expires_at.

nodes.label: Game profile JSON schema
nodes.rationale: Profiles are data outside the binary so users can add games without rebuilding; unknown discovery types degrade gracefully.

nodes.label: IPAM (10.200.<room>.0/24 via FNV-1a)
nodes.rationale: Subnet derived from room id so both sides compute it without negotiation; host is always .1 for a predictable gateway.

nodes.label: In-memory adapter backend
nodes.rationale: Deterministic adapter needing no driver or admin; daemon falls back to it so a room still works with an honest network.status.

nodes.label: Routing table / packet router
nodes.rationale: Never installs a default route; unknown destinations go to the hub; source-address mismatch dropped as Spoofed.

nodes.label: TAP-Windows6 driver 9.27.0
nodes.rationale: Installed only on demand; never removed on uninstall because it is shared with OpenVPN.

nodes.label: Plan B: TAP-Windows6 behind network.Adapter
nodes.rationale: Because the adapter sits behind an interface, true L2 is a new backend, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Known risk: Wintun is an L3 adapter
nodes.norm_label: known risk: wintun is an l3 adapter
nodes.rationale: Broadcast/multicast are Ethernet-level; an L3 TUN adapter may not deliver them, which threatens LAN discovery (e.g. Minecraft 224.0.0.251:4445).

nodes.label: NSIS installer build
nodes.rationale: NSIS only (no MSI) to keep one release artifact; doc says per-user while later docs say per-machine elevated install.

nodes.label: Wintun binding bugs (WintunStartSession arity, handles, DLL search)
nodes.norm_label: wintun binding bugs (wintunstartsession arity, handles, dll search)

nodes.label: Wintun Prebuilt Binaries License (WireGuard LLC)
nodes.rationale: Redistribution allowed only alongside software using the Permitted API (wintun.h).

nodes.label: Wintun driver 0.14.1 (vendored, SHA-256 pinned)
nodes.rationale: Checksum enforced so a DLL copied from another VPN cannot ship silently.

nodes.label: MTU 1200
nodes.rationale: Tunnel over arbitrary Internet paths cannot promise full-size frames.

nodes.label: App runs elevated (administrator)
nodes.rationale: Adapter creation needs admin; per-machine install keeps loaded binaries (wintun.dll) non-user-writable.

nodes.label: Mesh links (guest-to-guest direct)
nodes.rationale: Host relays offers/answers; receiver pins expected identity; failure falls back to host path.

nodes.label: Hub-and-spoke topology
nodes.rationale: Keeps NAT traversal to one negotiated pair per guest and relay logic in one place; host sees guest traffic (documented, not mitigated).

nodes.label: Tauri desktop shell (Rust)
nodes.rationale: Shell owns window, tray, autostart and sidecar lifecycle but implements no protocol logic except the graceful-stop hello+daemon.shutdown exchange.

nodes.label: Parent watch (no orphaned daemons, --managed-by-shell)
nodes.rationale: A Rust Drop guard was removed because forced kill skips unwind; the daemon polls its parent and stops itself instead.
